newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia allocates 3.8 mln barrels of Oct LSWR.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia allocates 3.8 mln barrels of Oct LSWR.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned Pertamina has allocated 3.8 million barrels of low sulphur waxy residue for lifting in October, industry soures said on Tuesday.
They said Pertamina issued the loading schedule on Monday but has yet to issue individual allocations to its four affiliates.
Only British Petroleum's allocation of 1.09 million barrels was confirmed, they said.
Sources said 1.8 million barrels will be for lifting from floating storage Platinum, 800,000 barrels from Balikpapan, 600,000 from Dumai, 400,000 from Sambu Jetty and 200,000 from Pakning.
While October's allocation is about 200,000 barrels higher than September's, some traders said lower regional demand might depress the premium over Pertamina's formula.
"Japan's demand season for LSWR is over," a Japanese trader said.
Japanese utilities consumption of the low sulphur burning fuel usually is at its seasonal peak during the hot summer months.
He estimated Japanese demand in October at 1 million barrels, down from the 1.2 million required in September.
He estimated South Korea demand would be around 750,000 barrels, Italy 560,000 barrels, India up to 400,000 barrels and Taiwan 250,000 barrels.
